references.text: The priest shall declare the person unclean when he examines leprosy, which establishes the priest's authority to pronounce uncleanness.
Describes the consequences for one declared leprous and unclean, including isolation from the camp.
Concerns the law for the leper on his day of cleansing, following the declaration of uncleanness.
The command to send unclean persons, including lepers, out of the camp.
Miriam was struck with leprosy and had to be shut outside the camp for seven days.
Naaman's leprosy was to cling to Gehazi and his descendants forever as punishment.
King Azariah (Uzziah) was struck with leprosy and lived in a house by himself.
King Uzziah became leprous on his forehead and had to live in isolation for the rest of his life.
Jesus heals a leper and sends him to the priest to show that he is clean, in accordance with the Law of Moses.
Jesus heals ten lepers and tells them to show themselves to the priests, referring to the priest's role in declaring cleanliness.
